title: Only my records: a Query Records filtered on the server by the signed-in user's id
description: A signed-in user's own rows, with the filter on the server (a server-side filter, the backend's where clause), not a Filter Records or a Function after the fetch. The Query Records node's `visualFilter` holds one rule, {"property": "owner", "operator": "equal to", "input": "owner"}, and that `input` mints the input port `qp-owner`; the User node's `id` is wired into it, so other users' rows never leave the server. `owner` is the backend's own field: it writes the creator's id into every record a signed-in user makes, from their session, and drops any `owner` a page sends, so the page that creates a Note sends no owner field at all. Never copy the user's id into a field of your own (an ownerId, a familyId, a teamId) to say whose a record is: that is the caller's word, and anyone signed in can send another id. Both fetch-at-build boxes are off (`runOnChange-collectionName` and `runOnChange-querySettings`: false) and Do is unwired: a rule whose qp- value has not arrived yet is dropped, so a query run before the id arrives would return every row the user may read; this way the id's arrival is what runs it. Sort and limit sit beside the filter (`visualSort`, `storageEnableLimit` + `storageLimit`). When a collection keeps its default creatorOwns rule and the backend enforces it, a user's query already returns only rows they own; the filter is how you narrow further, or how you ask for one person's rows in a shared collection.

nodes.label: One row per note of mine
